comparison: Both evaluations strongly support the immunoglobulin deposition findings (C3-C9, C16-C18). OpenEval emphasizes the quantitative robustness and multiple techniques, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm these as 'strong evidence' with no concerns raised. Peer review also includes C19 (complement co-localization) which OpenEval addresses separately in R2.

Perfect agreement on complement activation findings (C10-C13). Both evaluations find the evidence strong and well-supported through multiple techniques. OpenEval includes C19 and C62 here, while peer review focuses solely on the complement deposition claims.

Divergent evaluations of differential killing efficacy (C14-C15). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with minor caveats about local production hypothesis. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, accepting the differential killing but questioning whether the mechanism is truly antigen-specific versus Fc receptor-mediated, indicating concerns about interpretation.

Complete agreement on proteome array findings (C20-C28). Both evaluations support the autoantibody signature data. OpenEval notes the small sample size (n=5) as a limitation, while peer reviewers praise the methodology as 'state-of-the-art' without raising concerns.

Strong agreement on anti-bacterial antibody findings (C29-C32). Both evaluations support the E. coli proteome array data showing striking differences. Peer review notes the editor's suggestion for broader microbiota analysis, indicating the E. coli focus is somewhat limited but not incorrect.

Complete agreement on cross-reactivity evidence (C33-C35, C67). Both evaluations strongly support the capture-and-reprobe experimental design. Peer reviewers call this 'very interesting' and the editor affirms 'strong evidence' with no concerns raised.

Full agreement on GO enrichment analysis (C36-C39). Both evaluations support the subcellular targeting findings. OpenEval notes lack of explicit statistical thresholds, while peer reviewers praise the gene ontology assays as part of solid methodology without critique.

Agreement on bacterial antigen presence (C40-C41). Both evaluations support the IHC and LPS measurement findings. OpenEval includes C42 and C63 (mechanistic inferences), while peer review focuses only on the direct observations of bacterial products.

Partial agreement on local antibody production evidence (C43, C64). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes need for statistical details. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, accepting B/plasma cell presence but finding characterization incomplete, particularly regarding cell origin (gut-derived versus resident). Peer review includes C42 and C63 here, which OpenEval addresses in R8.

Divergent evaluations of mechanistic hypotheses (C46-C47, C51-C52, C72, C74). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of direct evidence for plasma cell migration and retention mechanisms. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, with reviewers calling it 'strong evidence' for the overall mechanism, though acknowledging some mechanistic details remain uncertain (B cell origin concern).

OpenEval addresses complement-mediated injury and prognostic claims (C45, C53-C54) as UNCERTAIN, noting causal links are inferred rather than proven. Peer review R10 focuses on the broader mechanistic model and rates it SUPPORTED, though with some reservations about details.

Divergent evaluations of therapeutic proposals (C75-C77). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative future directions lacking experimental validation. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, with reviewers accepting the translational implications and stating the data 'could add to future treatment options.'

Both evaluations support background and contextual claims (C1-C2, C48, C55, C62, C73 in OpenEval; broader set in peer R11). These represent established knowledge and appropriate citations that neither evaluation questions.

Both evaluations support prior published work citations (C49, C56-C60, C66, C68-C71). OpenEval groups these as literature context, while peer review includes them with other background claims. No concerns raised by either evaluation.
